title: Ambush & Containment: LLM API Weakpoints Brief
body:
Purpose:
This is a field-ready brief for reps and SEs to 'ambush' competitive conversations with LLM API vendors and then quickly 'contain' the deal into Redwood differentiation. Focus is on surfacing hidden tradeoffs (cost, reliability, deployment limits) and giving short, testable rebuttals plus a repeatable demo script for discovery calls.

Audience:
- AE/SE teams engaging mid-market to enterprise accounts
- Solution engineers prepping for technical deep-dive or PoC scoping

TL;DR Messaging (30s soundbites):
- "Many LLM APIs look identical on surface features; differences that matter for production are latency P99, predictable unit economics, and routing/fallback controls."
- "We help teams move from fragile ML endpoints to predictable inference with rollout controls, private deployment options, and cost levers that don’t degrade quality."

Three-layer Weakpoint Map (how to probe)
1) Product/Runtime Surface (ask and expose):
  - "How do you handle high tail latency spikes? P50/P95/P99 numbers by model and region? Do you throttle or queue and how are SLOs enforced?"
  - Hidden risk: vendors that only report average latency or synthetic microbenchmarks.
  - Redwood counter: present observed P99 reductions after prefix caching and continuous batching (demo metric: 3x fewer P99 spikes in multi-tenant tests).

2) Economics & Billing (probe to trap):
  - "What part of my bill varies with sequence length, KV cache usage, or warmup? How do you bill partial tokens on retries?"
  - Pricing trap: some vendors advertise low per-token rates but force heavy cold-start or per-request overheads; effective cost skyrockets for short-turn workloads.
  - Redwood counter: talk about per-route cost visibility, token-level breakdown, and committed capacity options to stabilize unit economics.

3) Operational & Compliance Surface (escalation lever):
  - "Can I deploy in our VPC/on-prem? How are audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations, and data residency handled?"
  - Trap: single-tenant promises that require re-architecting your network or introduce long lead times.
  - Redwood counter: point to Private offering and customer story where deployment occurred inside 6 weeks with KMS and audit pipelines intact.

Containment Question Flow (6-step discovery script):
1) SLO anchor: "What latency percentile must you meet for production?"
2) Cost anchor: "What is an acceptable $/1k token for this workload (including hidden overhead)?"
3) Deployment anchor: "Do you need VPC or on-prem for compliance?"
4) Failure mode: "What happens when your primary model hits capacity? Describe the fallback."
5) Observability: "Who owns trace-level visibility for inference errors and prompt regressions?"
6) Rollout: "How do you do canaries and rollbacks for model updates?"

Quick Rebuttal Stems (short scripts for reps):
- Prospect: "We already use VendorX and their latency is fine."
  - Reply: "What's your P99 and how often do you see >2x spikes? We typically see hidden tails when multi-tenant loads ramp; can we run a short synthetic test to compare?"
- Prospect: "Their price per token is lower."
  - Reply: "Let's look at your traffic shape — short-turn interactive vs long completions change effective cost dramatically. We can model your recent request trace to show the true $/1k."
- Prospect: "They support private deployment."
  - Reply: "Great — how long did their last private deployment take and what were the network requirements? We have a 6-week playbook we can share that keeps your audit controls intact."

Demo / PoC Play (15–30 minute technical triage)
- Prep (5m): ask for a small sample of production traces (anonymized): typical prompt lengths, rates, and percentiles.
- Synthetic run (10m): run a burst test across two model variants to show P50/P95/P99 divergence and effective cost per 1k tokens under your traffic shape.
- Observability snapshot (5m): show per-route tracing, retry rates, and token-level billing on the same trace.
- Outcome: provide a one-page cost/latency delta and recommended rollout plan.

Top Competitive Traps to Set (examples to surface)
- Pricing complexity: highlight billing rules that charge for both input+output and per-request overhead for retries.
- Model compatibility: vendors that lock customers into custom SDKs or non-standard APIs (migration risk).
- Slow fallbacks: when primary model saturates, slow fallback that increases latency by 3–10x.
- Hidden quotas: soft limits that require manual support escalation to increase.

Data Points & Benchmarks (field-usable)
- Typical Redwood observed numbers (internal bench): P50 60–90ms, P95 200–300ms, P99 spikes reduced by 60% after prefix/KV caching on common 2–8 token completion workloads.
- Example effective cost heuristic: if median sequence length <20 tokens, per-request overhead dominates; invoice can be 2–4x worse than headline per-token rate depending on vendor.

Escalation & Legal Levers (when technical rebuttal isn't enough)
- Ask for SLA language: uptime, latency SLOs, and credits for missed SLOs.
- For procurement stalls: request a short-term Dedicated trial with committed capacity to show predictable throughput.
- Compliance push: ask their security lead for SOC/ISO artifacts; if missing, escalate to product security and offer Redwood Private as a mitigation.

Don't Say / Avoid (frame language traps)
- Don’t claim "best model quality" without an eval tied to the customer's prompt set.
- Don’t use comparative pricing claims without a modeled trace — always qualify with "based on the workload you've shared."

Suggested Assets to Attach in Outreach
- One-pager: "Predictable Inference Economics" (attach after PoC)
- Short deck: "Latency Tail & Real Cost" (3 slides: problem, demo screenshot, recommendation)
- Tracing snippet: small anonymized trace comparison (CSV)

Follow-up Template (email after demo)
Subject: "Latency & Cost snapshot from today — next steps"
Hi <name>,
Thanks for the call — attached is the short snapshot comparing P50/P95/P99 and effective $/1k on your trace. Proposed next step: 2-week Dedicated trial that mirrors your traffic shape (we'll scope today).
Cheers,
<Priya or SE>

Notes & Next Edits:
- Add customer anonymized case study for compliance-heavy PoC (requested from solutions team).
- Add a short checklist for Field SE to collect network firewall rules pre-demo.
- Validate the cost heuristics with Finance before including in external materials.

Quick reference tickets: CONFLUENCE-4821 (benchmarking playbook), GTMT-842 (field enablement).

End of brief.
